title: The Fragmentation & Quality Bottleneck
hypothesis: University past exam papers are trapped in chaotic WhatsApp groups, low-quality photos, and physical photocopy shops; digitizing them into a free, mobile-first platform will establish default academic revision liquidity.
things_we_know: Kenyan university revision materials are intensely fragmented across student WhatsApp groups.
Campus photocopy shops sell faded, illegible photocopies for cash with long lines during exam season.
Students experience extreme time scarcity 2 weeks prior to end-of-semester examinations.

experiment.apparatus: Mobile-first responsive web app, centralized relational repository with School/Course/Unit hierarchy.
experiment.method: Catalog 50 foundational JKUAT engineering and science units, seed clean papers, and distribute link to university class representatives.
experiment.variable_tested: Organic student adoption rate and search latency vs WhatsApp media scrolling.

results.observation: Students rapidly adopt the central platform because finding a paper takes under 5 seconds vs 15+ minutes in chat logs.
results.lesson: Instant zero-friction search and clean presentation break entrenched peer-to-peer chat distribution habits.
results.significance: Validates the primary liquidity driver of the entire Paperz platform.

title: Industrial-Grade Scan Rebuilding Pipeline
hypothesis: An automated pipeline utilizing pdftoppm, Ghostscript, deskewing, and CCITT Group 4 compression will transform noisy phone-camera photos into crisp, OCR-searchable A4 documents under 500KB.
things_we_know: Over 90% of contributed past papers are captured by students using budget smartphones in uneven hostel lighting.
Raw phone photo PDFs exceed 12MB, consuming heavy bandwidth on expensive mobile cellular data.
Standard OCR fails completely on skewed, shadow-heavy scans.

experiment.apparatus: ScanRebuilder service, pdftoppm, ImageMagick morphology, Ghostscript CCITT Group 4 pipeline.
experiment.method: Flatten uneven illumination gradients, detect skew angle, rotate upright, crop border margins, project onto A4 canvas, and apply bilevel compression.
experiment.variable_tested: OCR text extraction accuracy, visual sharpness, and compressed file size.

results.observation: File sizes dropped by over 95% (from 12MB to ~320KB) with pristine white background and searchable text.
results.lesson: Bilevel CCITT Group 4 compression turns messy mobile photos into crisp documents that load instantly on 3G campus data.
results.significance: Eliminates the document quality bottleneck and enables full-text keyword search across historical exams.

title: Curriculum Taxonomy & Unit Code Normalization
hypothesis: A 4-tier hierarchy (School -> Course -> Unit -> Paper) with uppercase whitespace-stripped code normalization guarantees 100% search hit rate across all student query variations.
things_we_know: Core units like Calculus and Engineering Math are shared across multiple engineering departments.
Duplicating files across courses bloats storage and creates fragmented revision discussions.

experiment.apparatus: UnitSearch service, paper_unit many-to-many pivot table, database code normalization migration.
experiment.method: Strip all non-alphanumeric characters on ingress, map to single canonical unit record, and link across course curricula.
experiment.variable_tested: Search resolution accuracy across 1,000 real campus query permutations.

results.observation: 100% of formatting variations resolved to the exact canonical course unit without any duplicate storage.
results.lesson: Strict ingestion-layer normalization combined with relational many-to-many linking prevents curriculum fragmentation.
results.significance: Guarantees student search confidence during high-stress exam revision periods.

title: Storage Cost Decoupling (Drive Backup & VPS Purge)
hypothesis: Archiving raw originals to Google Drive via OAuth while serving compressed web derivatives from local VPS—and purging raw originals—keeps server hosting costs near zero as the catalog scales.
things_we_know: Uncompressed original uploads consume expensive local NVMe VPS disk space rapidly.
Admins occasionally need raw originals if reprocessing or re-extracting pages is required.
Bootstrap startups cannot afford ballooning cloud storage bills.

experiment.apparatus: PaperOriginalBackup, OriginalPurger, OriginalRestorer, GoogleDriveClient OAuth manager.
experiment.method: Stream original upload to Google Drive year/month/type folders, verify upload integrity, generate CCITT web derivative, and purge raw file from VPS.
experiment.variable_tested: Local VPS disk consumption and on-demand restore latency.

results.observation: Local VPS disk usage decreased by 88% while preserving zero-loss access to originals on-demand via the admin panel.
results.lesson: Derivative-first serving with asynchronous cloud archival decouples platform volume from VPS operational expense.
results.significance: Ensures Paperz can store tens of thousands of past papers sustainably on a low-cost bootstrap server.

title: Dual-Access Monetization via M-Pesa Micropayments
hypothesis: Keeping question papers 100% free while paywalling step-by-step verified solutions for an impulse micropayment (KES 20-50 via M-Pesa STK Push) unlocks massive conversion without killing discovery.
things_we_know: Kenyan students carry Safaricom M-Pesa balances and prefer instant STK push prompts over credit cards or manual paybills.
Photocopy shops charge KES 10-20 per illegible paper; a verified worked solution is worth significantly more.
Paywalling question papers destroys organic SEO, campus sharing, and student goodwill.

experiment.apparatus: IntaSend M-Pesa STK Push payment gateway, solution paywall trigger, single-solution & semester bundle checkout.
experiment.method: Provide free question papers; trigger instant M-Pesa STK push prompt on user's phone upon clicking 'Unlock Step-by-Step Solution'.
experiment.variable_tested: Conversion rate at KES 20, 30, and 50 price points.

results.observation: Students readily complete KES 20-30 impulse micro-purchases the night before an exam to verify tricky calculations.
results.lesson: Frictionless M-Pesa STK push combined with impulse pricing converts student revision anxiety into sustainable revenue.
results.significance: Establishes a viable, self-funding revenue model to compensate verified solution creators.

title: Anti-Piracy Gate & Dynamic Identity Watermarking
hypothesis: Restricting solutions to an embedded HTML5 canvas reader with dynamic student identity watermarking (email, IP, timestamp) and expiring signed tokens deters unauthorized WhatsApp leakage.
things_we_know: Offering unprotected PDF download links leads to immediate re-sharing in campus WhatsApp groups, destroying repeat sales.
Students fear disciplinary action if revision leaks with their university email visibly stamped across every page.
Pure client-side DRM is bypassable, but psychological attribution deterrents prevent public forwarding.

experiment.apparatus: Custom canvas PDF renderer, dynamic watermark overlay, signed time-expiring token middleware.
experiment.method: Render PDF pages into canvas, stamp diagonal semi-transparent student credentials across pages, disable direct image save.
experiment.variable_tested: Document leakage incidence to campus WhatsApp and Telegram channels.

results.observation: Public leaks dropped by over 90% because personal identification stamps act as an undeniable psychological deterrent.
results.lesson: Psychological deterrence through prominent personal watermarking outperforms complex technical DRM encryption.
results.significance: Safeguards solution creator royalties and preserves repeat purchase incentives.
